title: Theona — Three Greens, No Ninth
label: chap:theona

overview.tagline: The Green Host rides for those who count to nine. Viterra counts to nine. The Everflame burns the ninth. The Gray Liturgy rings the ninth — and waits to see what answers.
overview.genre: Celtic folk horror, syncretic faith, occupied islands, fae bargains, ninth-taboo tension between four law-codes.
overview.mood: Three Greens, No Ninth — and a gray thread waiting at the threshold.
overview.starting_location: A Moot Hill under rain, where vows are carved into standing stone and blackthorn knives gleam beside the ogham pillar. A Bride-Peacemaker draws a blade between two bloodlines. "The ninth vow was never spoken," she says. "But the Green Host remembers. Bring us the head of the slaver who burned the eastern strand, and the feud will end. Fail, and your name will join the uncounted. Or the sheriff will take you for vagrancy — the crown has declared our moots unlawful assemblies. Or the Abbess will call it heresy. Or, if you listen closely, the Confessor's bell will ring for you. The bell has not rung in seven years. She is waiting."

lore.history: The isles of Theona rise green and jagged from the Dolmis, their basalt cliffs wrapped in mists and moorland song. Nominally a duchy sworn to Viterra, in truth the Three Greens heed no crown but their own moots, no law but their taboos. The greatest of these is the silence of Nine: no bell tolls a ninth, no bridge counts that span, no oath dares its syllable. It is said that those who break the ban invite the Green Host — the Aos Sí, the elder folk who were here before the first Viterran longship. The Viterran crown claims the isles by right of conquest and papal bull. Its sheriffs impose common law, its bishops raise stone steeples. But the Church of the Everflame watches from Whiterick Abbey. The Abbess schemes to preserve power by pitting Viterra, the native factions, and raiders against each other, seeking to purge the 'pagan' taboos and impose imperial orthodoxy. And in the mist, a quieter power waits: the Gray Liturgy. Its Confessors carry the weight of the dead; its Gray Walkers guide the dying across; its Well-Walkers descend into the Ninth and return. It offers no gold, no land, no writs — only a gray thread and a cracked bell. For those who have lost too much, that is enough. To break a taboo is to invite not only the fae but the inquisitor. The sheriff leaves a noose. The Host leaves a hollow in the mist where your name used to be. The Abbess leaves a brand that burns until confession. The Confessor leaves a thread — and a question.
lore.first_notice: The smell of wet peat and salt. The silence that follows every eighth bell-ring. The hawthorn and blackthorn trees at every crossroads — the fairy thorns that no local will touch, and that Viterran surveyors learn to skirt after the first one disappears. The gray threads on the wrists of those who carry weight.
lore.rule_that_kills: Never pour the ninth cup at a feast. Never speak the ninth name in a bargain. Never step where a step is missing. The Green Host rides for those who complete what should remain incomplete. The Viterran sheriff will hang you for the same offense — but the Host takes your name, not your neck. The Everflame Inquisitor will burn you for the silence itself. The Confessor will ring for you once, and the dead will listen.

entanglements.east: Viterra — across the narrow sound, the crown sharpens its taxes and its nooses.
entanglements.north: Linn — dragon-prows cut through the fog for raiding.
entanglements.south: Zakov & the Vilikari shore — pirates trade stolen goods for kelp and salt; Ashaani slavers hunt the coves in stolen coracles.
entanglements.west: Aelinnel & Aelaerem — Sidhi sailors and Aelinnel factors run cargo up the tide-stairs; Aelaerem hedge-wives barter red thread for hawthorn passes.

regional_diagnostic.current_hook: The Green Host rides for those who count to nine. Viterra counts to nine. The Everflame burns the ninth. The Gray Liturgy rings the ninth — and waits to see what answers.
regional_diagnostic.core_conflict: Players are caught between the **Viterran crown's** common law, the **Everflame's** Inquisition, the **moots' and Green Host's** taboo of Nine, and the **Gray Liturgy's** patient threshold-waiting — each demanding a different relationship to the Ninth, and each offering a different price for protection.
regional_diagnostic.unique_feature: **The Silent Count:** no bell tolls a ninth, no bridge counts its span aloud, no oath dares its final syllable. Omitting the ninth thing is how the isles evade Viterran law and Everflame orthodoxy alike. The Gray Liturgy approaches the Ninth deliberately — its taboo-breakers have heard An Caillte knock, and lived to tell of it, carefully, and only once.
regional_diagnostic.ninth_taboo: The ninth cup, the ninth name, the ninth step where a step is missing — each draws the Green Host's attention. The Host takes your name, not your neck. Speak the silence aloud instead and the Everflame will brand you for heresy; complete the count under Viterran eyes and the sheriff will hang you regardless. Tie a gray thread instead, and the Confessor will ring for you — and the dead will listen.
regional_diagnostic.price: Players sacrifice **names, memory, or standing among the moots** to gain power here. Every blessing or writ invites scrutiny from the sheriff, the Abbess, the Host — or the Gray Liturgy's patient questions.

faction_triad.goal: Stretch the queen's shadow across the Three Greens — plantation, common law, tax-rolls
faction_triad.why_players_care: Crown writs are the only claims the outside world recognizes

faction_triad.faction: The Church of the Everflame (Whiterick Abbey)
faction_triad.goal: Purge the old taboos and impose orthodoxy
faction_triad.method: Inquisitors, censers, brands — while secretly arming raiders to keep crown and moots off balance
faction_triad.why_players_care: The Abbess's schemes touch every faction, often without their knowledge

faction_triad.faction: The Moots, the Matron, and the Green Host
faction_triad.goal: Preserve Brehon law, guest-right, and the silence of Nine
faction_triad.method: Cairn votes, wergild, blood-price — and the Host's long, patient memory
faction_triad.why_players_care: Breaking a taboo costs your name, not just your neck; the moots' favor is the only protection that outlasts a change of governor

faction_triad.faction: The Gray Liturgy (Confessors, Gray Walkers, Taboo-Breakers)
faction_triad.goal: Witness the Ninth and carry its weight
faction_triad.method: Bell-ringing, keening, gray threads, and the patient silence of the dead
faction_triad.why_players_care: They offer a third way — not evasion, not confrontation, but carrying what cannot be forgotten

ninth_taboo.description: No bell tolls a ninth. No bridge counts its span aloud. No oath dares its ninth syllable. Those who complete a ninth — a ninth cup poured, a ninth name spoken, a ninth step taken where a step is missing — draw the attention of the Green Host, the Aos Sí who rode these isles before the first Viterran longship. The Host does not kill. It takes the name: the victim is still seen, still spoken to, still fed at table, but no one — including themselves — can any longer recall what to call them. Only the Gray Liturgy approaches the Ninth deliberately: its taboo-breakers (Caillteoirí) have heard An Caillte, the Lost Saint, knock — and lived to tell of it, carefully, and only once.

quotes.speaker: Abbess Caelia of Whiterick (Everflame)
quotes.text: The Viterran sheriffs count heads for tax. The Moot-keepers count steps for safety. I count souls for salvation. Nine is a sin. Eight is a compromise. Only the Flame is whole. The Gray Liturgy is a sickness that must be burned out — not because it is wrong, but because it remembers what I have chosen to forget.

quotes.speaker: Matron of Wells (Theona)
quotes.text: The wells here hold more than water — they hold the dreams and the breath of generations. The Viterran sheriffs call it superstition. The Abbess calls it heresy. The Green Host calls it trespass. The Confessor calls it the only truth she can carry. I have never been able to disagree with any of them, and so I keep the wells.

quotes.speaker: Bríd, the Bride-Peacemaker
quotes.text: The ninth vow was never spoken. But the Green Host remembers. The crown has writs for everything else, but no writ for a vow you didn't speak. The Gray Liturgy has a thread for it. I've seen them tied. I've never seen one cut.

quotes.speaker: Confessor of the Eastern Shore (Gray Liturgy)
quotes.text: I ring my bell when a burden is too heavy to carry alone. I ring it when the dead have something to say. I ring it when the Green Host rides and I can hear the name they are taking. I have not rung it in seven years. I am waiting for someone to bring me a weight worth carrying.

npcs.name: Matron Eithne
npcs.motivation: Preserve the old ways against Viterran and Everflame encroachment
npcs.quirk: She drinks only from the ninth well — the one no voice names. The crown declared it a nuisance; the Abbess declared it a font of demons. The water still flows, and it tastes of iron and old songs. She has never heard the Confessor's bell. She does not need to.

npcs.name: King Conall
npcs.role: Three-Isles King, elected by the moots
npcs.motivation: Walk the narrow causeway between Viterra's law, the Everflame's orthodoxy, and the old taboos
npcs.quirk: He lost his left hand to a Linn raid; the replacement is carved from hawthorn. He signs Viterran writs with the false hand — the signatures are legally binding; he is not. The Abbess refuses to shake it. The Gray Liturgy offered him a thread once; he declined, and has regretted it ever since.

npcs.name: Bríd
npcs.motivation: End feuds before the Green Host rides or the Inquisitors intervene
npcs.quirk: Her knife has a wooden blade; families cut their palms with wood, blood without iron. She has never lost a client to Viterran justice. She has never explained why families trust a wooden blade more than iron. She ties a gray thread around the hands of the wed. The knot never loosens.

npcs.name: Sister Cera
npcs.role: Missionary of the Temple of Light (Viterra)
npcs.motivation: Convert the islanders to the White Flame through gentle persuasion
npcs.quirk: She preaches in the old tongue and leaves offerings at hawthorn groves. The bishop calls her a traitor; the Abbess calls her weak; the Confessor calls her patient. She carries a gray thread in her pocket, though she does not know why.

npcs.name: Brother Iarlath
npcs.motivation: Purge the 'pagan' taboos and impose imperial orthodoxy; serve the Abbess
npcs.quirk: His censer never cools, but it smokes green in the fog. He has condemned nine hawthorn sentinels to burning. Eight burned. The ninth vanished overnight. He blames the Host. The Gray Liturgy left a thread where the ninth sentinel stood. He cannot bring himself to touch it.

npcs.name: Abbess Caelia
npcs.motivation: Preserve Everflame power by pitting Viterra, the natives, and the raiders against one another
npcs.quirk: She never counts aloud. Her rosary has eight beads; the ninth is a hidden blade. She funds the raiders who harass the Viterran ships. She has heard the Confessor's bell once, and has not slept since. The Gray Liturgy sent her a thread; she burned it, and the fire burned her hand.

npcs.name: Sheriff Markham
npcs.motivation: Stretch the queen's shadow across the Three Greens
npcs.quirk: He carries the Statutes of Kilkenny and has never read them; he uses them to beat witnesses. He limps slightly and blames a boot that never fit right; the limp started the week he arrested a hawthorn sentinel. He woke the next day with a gray thread tied around his ankle and no memory of tying it.

npcs.name: The Lady Beneath
npcs.motivation: Keep the old pacts and claim the ninth name
npcs.quirk: She has no face. Those who see her forget their own name for a year and answer only to 'John.' The Abbess calls her a demon prince; the Confessor calls her a bell that has not yet been rung. The Gray Liturgy does not name her. They leave threads at her hollows and wait.

npcs.name: Clogaire Malla
npcs.role: Confessor of the Eastern Shore (Gray Liturgy)
npcs.motivation: Carry the weight of the dead who die badly
npcs.quirk: Her hands are scarred from ringing. She has not rung her bell in seven years — she is waiting, and will not say for what. The Abbess once tried to buy her silence; the gold turned to ash. The Gray Liturgy keeps her fed; she does not need much.

npcs.name: Tréadaí Eamon
npcs.role: Gray Walker of the Fog-Wick Tower
npcs.motivation: Guide the dying and sing the keening
npcs.quirk: His lantern carries a single gray flame he never lit — he found it already burning. The bishop declared it a pagan light and tried to extinguish it. The flame did not notice. He sings the keening for the dead, and the dead follow. He has never lost a soul to the fog.

places.title: Tide-Stairs
places.subtitle: [RUIN] [OMEN]
places.description: Basalt steps into a cove; everyone skips the 'missing' rung.
places.flavor: The missing step is still there — you just can't see it. Step where it should be, or don't step at all. The first Viterran engineer counted nine rungs aloud. He is still counting, somewhere in the fog. The Abbess tried to fill the gap with stone; the stone sank. The Confessor tied a gray thread to the missing step. The thread is still there. It has never faded.
places.mechanical_hook: A character who deliberately steps where the ninth rung should be must test Resolve (DV 4) or tick the **Green Host Rising** timer by 1. Tying a gray thread to the step instead (Superstitions) avoids the tick entirely and grants the Confessor's attention (+1 die on the next Spirit-related roll).

places.title: Saint's Well
places.subtitle: [FAITH] [OMEN]
places.description: Under hawthorn hung with ribbons and secrets; wishes tied in cloth.
places.flavor: The ribbons are knotted in eights. The ninth knot is never tied — only imagined. The crown calls it idolatry. The Abbess calls it witchcraft. The water tastes of iron and old tongues. The Confessors drink from it before they ring; the Gray Walkers leave a thread at its edge and do not explain why.
places.mechanical_hook: Drinking before a Rite or ritual act grants +1 die, but tying a ninth ribbon (rather than an eighth) ticks the Green Host Rising timer by 1 — see **Theona Superstitions**. A gray thread tied instead does not tick the timer and grants a Confessor's attention.

places.title: Fog-Wick Tower
places.subtitle: [FAITH] [MYSTERY]
places.description: Burning peat; the bell plays eight notes, never nine.
places.flavor: The bell-ringer wears a mask. Underneath, he has no mouth — only a whisper. The sheriff has tried to arrest him three times; each time, the tower was empty. The Inquisitor tried to silence the bell; it rang in his head instead. The Tréadaí lights his lantern at the tower and never speaks to the ringer. They understand each other. The Gray Liturgy sends its Confessors to the tower; they ring once, in silence, and the bell remembers.
places.mechanical_hook: Resting at the tower clears 1 Fatigue, but a character who tries to make the bell play a ninth note must test Resolve (DV 4) or gain the Condition **Marked by Silence** (–1 die on all Sway rolls until cleared by a Confessor). A Confessor may clear the Condition by ringing their own bell.

places.title: Black Bog Causeway
places.subtitle: [TRAVEL] [OMEN]
places.description: White stones like teeth; will-lights test your stride.
places.flavor: The stones were set by a king who drowned; he counts each footstep from below. Viterran surveyors replaced the stones with wooden posts — the posts burned. The Abbess claims the bog is consecrated ground; it isn't. The Confessor walks the causeway backward, saying the stones are easier to count in reverse. The Gray Walkers cross it at dusk, singing the keening so the will-lights mistake them for the dead.
places.mechanical_hook: Crossing requires an Athletics or Endurance roll (DV 4); a Miss draws a **Bog-Light** complication (see Complications, rank 2). A character singing the keening (Spirit+Performance DV 3) may cancel the complication entirely, but the Gray Liturgy will notice.

places.title: Cliff Ringfort
places.subtitle: [FORTIFICATION] [DANGER]
places.description: Over kelp-nets; storm-ladders creak like hymns.
places.flavor: The ladders are hauled up at dusk. If you're left below, you sleep with the tide. The crown calls it a 'fortified dwelling without license'; it has never needed one. The Everflame wants to build a chapel there — the chapel slides into the sea. The Gray Liturgy built a bell-shrine on the cliff instead. The fort still stands. The Confessor rings her bell from the shrine, and the fort remembers.
places.mechanical_hook: Arriving after dusk without prior arrangement forces an Athletics roll (DV 5) to climb before the tide rises, or the party is stranded below until morning. A gray thread tied to the ladder before climbing grants +1 die to the roll — the Confessor is watching.

places.title: Barrow Field
places.subtitle: [RUIN] [OMEN]
places.description: Standing stones; birds hush at noon, the earth remembers.
places.flavor: The stones have ears. Do not speak a secret you cannot bear to lose. The gorse hums with bees that should not be awake. A Viterran antiquary who tried to excavate one now tends the barrow as a shrine and does not remember why. The Abbess's exorcism wrote itself on the stones. The Confessor's bell rang at midnight there. The stones listened. The Gray Walkers leave a thread at each stone, and the threads do not fade.
places.mechanical_hook: Speaking a genuine secret aloud within the field grants +1 Boon (the earth 'remembers' it for you, freeing your mind), but the GM may reveal that secret to an NPC later at a dramatically inconvenient time. A gray thread tied to a stone keeps the secret safe for a session without cost.

places.title: Sea-Cave Harp
places.subtitle: [FAE] [MYSTERY]
places.description: Tide-ropes sing under a headland; echoes bargain for safe passage.
places.flavor: The harp has no player. It plays itself when the drowned want to speak. The crown's notices against 'unauthorized musical performances' wash away. The Abbess calls the music a siren song, and listens anyway. The Tréadaí sings the keening with the harp; the drowned listen. The Confessor rings her bell to the harp's rhythm, and the drowned answer with a single note.
places.mechanical_hook: Listening in silence for one scene grants a genuine secret from the drowned (GM's choice), but singing along without invitation risks drawing the attention of whatever the drowned are still bargaining with — treat as a Desperate Insight roll (DV 4). A gray thread tied to a tide-rope grants +1 die to the roll.

places.title: Uncounted Bridge
places.subtitle: [TABOO] [OMEN]
places.flavor: The ninth arch is there — but the locals will deny it. Walk it at your own risk. A Viterran cartographer's map now shows a bridge to nowhere. The Abbess's blessing of the ninth arch curdled. The Confessor rings her bell on the ninth arch, and the arch remembers. The Gray Liturgy leaves a thread on the ninth arch, and the thread does not fray.
places.mechanical_hook: Crossing via the ninth arch (rather than detouring) shortens travel time by one segment on any relevant timer, but ticks the **Green Host Rising** timer by 1. A gray thread tied to the arch before crossing avoids the tick.

places.title: Ogham Grove
places.subtitle: [RUIN] [CURSE]
places.description: Carved pillars around an absent ninth post; runes speak in silence.
places.flavor: The missing post was a king's vow carved in heartwood; the runes still curse his line. Axes broke trying to fell the grove; fire sent to burn it turned green. Taboo-Breakers say the runes of the missing post are still there — you simply cannot see them. The Gray Liturgy keeps the grove; its Taboo-Breakers know the runes that cannot be seen.
places.mechanical_hook: A character with Lore trained may attempt to 'read' the absent post (Wits+Lore, DV 5); success reveals a genuine piece of Theonan history or a hook of the GM's choosing. A gray thread tied to a visible post grants +1 die to the roll — the Confessor has already read the invisible runes and will share if asked.

places.title: Coracle Harbor
places.subtitle: [TRADE] [REFUGE]
places.description: Jammed in a notch; upturned boats roof the sheds.
places.flavor: The coracles are made of hide and guilt — each one has carried a secret. The harbormaster pays no tax; the crown cannot find him, the Abbess cannot buy him. The Confessor has a coracle. She rows it without oars. The tide moves her. The Gray Walkers launch from the harbor at dusk, carrying lanterns with gray flames — the tide carries them too.
places.mechanical_hook: Sheltering here grants a free night's refuge from crown or Abbey pursuit, but the harbormaster expects a story or a secret in payment — refusing costs 1 Supply instead. A gray thread left with the harbormaster ensures safe passage for a season.

places.title: Green Moot Hill
places.subtitle: [LAW] [ASSEMBLY]
places.description: The Three Greens' court; benches of turf, salt wind judges.
places.flavor: The wind never stops. It carries the votes of the dead. The Viterran sheriff who declared the moot an 'illegal assembly' has not returned since the wind took his hat. The Abbess's clerk recorded his own confession instead of the votes. The Tréadaí sings the keening at the moot's close, and the dead vote. The Confessor rings her bell at the moot's opening, and the wind listens.
places.mechanical_hook: A Brehon judgment rendered here is binding under old law and grants +1 die to any future social roll invoking it; raiding the moot in session risks a Cap 3 crowd united against the raiders. A gray thread tied to the judgment stone ensures the dead vote true.

places.title: High Hall
places.subtitle: [AUTHORITY] [RITUAL]
places.description: Whale-rib beams; storm banners sleep, kings are chosen.
places.flavor: Kings are chosen by lot — a knotted cord pulled from a pot with eight knots. The crown's appointed governor was once given the ninth knot; it came undone. The Abbess's golden cord strangled its bearer. The Confessor rings her bell when the king is chosen, and the king remembers. The Gray Liturgy leaves a thread at the king's chair; the kings who ignore it do not reign long.
places.mechanical_hook: Witnessing a king's choosing grants a String on King Conall or a rival claimant, usable once during the campaign. A gray thread tied to the cord before drawing grants +1 die to the selection roll.

places.title: Lookout Cliff
places.subtitle: [OMEN] [VISTA]
places.description: One vantage where all three isles stand in a single gaze.
places.flavor: From here, you can see the Green Host riding on the horizon — if it wants you to. You can see the Viterran garrison on the far isle; they do not wave. You can see Whiterick Abbey's smoke, always green. You can see the Confessor's bell-shrine. The bell is ringing. You cannot hear it. The Gray Walkers stand here at dusk, lighting their gray lanterns — the light reaches the dead, and the dead see it.
places.mechanical_hook: Standing here at dusk lets a character ask the GM one true fact about the current state of any of the three powers (crown, church, moots) — but the GM may choose which fact to answer, not the player. A gray thread tied to the cliff's edge before asking ensures the answer is true.

people_and_factions.title: Peat-Cutter
people_and_factions.subtitle: [COMMONER] [SECRETS]
people_and_factions.description: Steady barrow, steadier gossip; knows every hidden path.
people_and_factions.flavor: Her barrow has a false bottom. She hides keepsakes there — and the tax collector when he comes; he is always grateful. She hides Inquisitors too; they are less grateful. She counts every coin the barrow ever hid, aloud, in her sleep. She leaves a gray thread at the corner of her barrow every new moon. The Confessor knows where it is.
people_and_factions.debt: She'll guide the party past a checkpoint or patrol once, if they don't ask what else she's hiding.
people_and_factions.price: A keepsake worth hiding, or a secret worth keeping.

people_and_factions.title: Well-Keeper
people_and_factions.subtitle: [FAITH] [FEUD]
people_and_factions.description: Ties ribbons, unknots feuds; wishes and wisdom in equal measure.
people_and_factions.flavor: She never ties a ninth ribbon — the ninth wish is always her own. She has wished for the sheriff's departure every day for seven years; he is still here. She leaves a ribbon at the Confessor's bell-shrine. The bell rings. The wish is heard. She also ties gray threads for those who carry weight the ribbons cannot hold.
people_and_factions.debt: She'll tie a blessing-ribbon for the party (as a Superstition-style boon) in exchange for news of the wider isles.
people_and_factions.price: A true wish, spoken aloud and meant.

people_and_factions.title: Kelp-Netter
people_and_factions.subtitle: [COMMONER] [SEA]
people_and_factions.description: Reads rip lines like currents; tide as teacher.
people_and_factions.flavor: His net has a torn patch, sewn with thread from a hanged horse-thief's shirt. The net has never torn again. The thread glows near Everflame steel. He won't fish past dusk, not since the net came up heavier than anything it should have caught. He ties a gray thread to the torn patch every season. The thread never rots.
people_and_factions.debt: He'll ferry the party through dangerous currents safely, once, in exchange for help mending nets or gear.
people_and_factions.price: A day's honest labor, or information about Everflame movements along the coast.

people_and_factions.title: Harp-Satirist
people_and_factions.subtitle: [COMMONER] [WEAPON]
people_and_factions.description: A few bars can end a career or a war; music as a weapon.
people_and_factions.flavor: Her harp is strung with catgut and grudges — each string is a name. She has a string for the sheriff, unplayed. She has a new string for the Abbess; it hums when the censer smokes. She played a note for the Confessor once. The bell answered. She will not play it again. She has a gray thread tied to the harp's neck; the Confessor gave it to her, and she plays truer since.
people_and_factions.debt: She'll compose a satire to humiliate a named rival, once, if the target genuinely deserves it.
people_and_factions.price: A true story about the target — verified, not rumor.

people_and_factions.title: Wick-Warden
people_and_factions.subtitle: [FAITH] [GUARDIAN]
people_and_factions.description: Tends fog-lamps, counts in eights; guardian of the silent count.
people_and_factions.flavor: He counts on his fingers — thumb, finger, finger, finger — and stops. The ninth is for the fog. He taught the Viterran lighthouse keeper to count; the keeper lost his job. He lights a lamp for the Tréadaí, who lights his lantern from it. They have never spoken. He leaves a gray thread at the base of every lamp he tends; the Confessor collects them, and the lamps burn brighter.
people_and_factions.debt: He'll teach the Silent Count properly to anyone who tends a fog-lamp with him for a night.
people_and_factions.price: A night's vigil, and a promise never to count past eight in his presence.

people_and_factions.title: Taboo-Witness
people_and_factions.subtitle: [LAW] [FAITH]
people_and_factions.description: Geas-keeper who knows which words ruin deals.
people_and_factions.flavor: She carries a bell with no clapper and rings it with her tongue. A Viterran magistrate withdrew a charge after she rang it once. An Inquisitor confessed his own sins after she rang it again. She rings her bell when the Confessor rings hers. The sound is the same. She wears a gray thread around her wrist — the Confessor tied it, and she has not cut it.
people_and_factions.debt: She'll sit in on any negotiation as a neutral witness, catching any spoken taboo before it triggers — for a fee.
people_and_factions.price: 1 Supply, or a secret about the party's own dealings, told honestly.

people_and_factions.title: Island Abbot
people_and_factions.subtitle: [FAITH] [TOLERANCE]
people_and_factions.description: Saint's bell, tolerant smile; faith in the old ways.
people_and_factions.flavor: His bell rings eight times; the ninth ring is the silence that follows. He burned the bishop's letter of censure for kindling and used the Abbess's letter of conversion to wrap cheese. The bell has rung truer since he stopped asking why the bishop's letters kept vanishing. He leaves a gray thread at the foot of his bell every morning; the Confessor has never taken one.
people_and_factions.debt: He'll shelter fugitives from both crown and Abbey, quietly, so long as they respect his eight-count.
people_and_factions.price: Honest confession of why you need shelter — he will not press further.

people_and_factions.title: Green Neighbor
people_and_factions.subtitle: [FAE] [OMEN]
people_and_factions.description: Polite emissary from under the hill; borrowed boots, strange customs.
people_and_factions.flavor: He never steps on a crack; the earth has teeth. A Viterran tax assessor who stepped on one now has a limp. An Everflame envoy who did now preaches a gospel of dirt. He stops every count at eight, mid-word, without seeming to notice he's done it. He does not touch gray threads; the Host does not claim what is already witnessed.
people_and_factions.debt: He'll broker a minor bargain with the Green Host on the party's behalf, once, if approached with proper respect.
people_and_factions.price: A gift left at a hawthorn crossroads — never coin, always something handmade.

people_and_factions.title: Coracle-Captain
people_and_factions.subtitle: [TRADE] [FAE]
people_and_factions.description: Eight-boat flotilla; swift as rumor, sure as the tide.
people_and_factions.flavor: Her boats have no names — naming a vessel invites the Green Host to count it. A Viterran harbormaster who tried to register one could not find it, though it was right in front of him. Every prow is carved smooth where a name should be. She says a boat doesn't need one to know where it's going. She ties a gray thread to each prow; the Confessor has never asked why.
people_and_factions.debt: She'll smuggle the party or their cargo past any checkpoint, once, if they don't ask about her other cargo.
people_and_factions.price: A cut of whatever's being moved, and total discretion afterward.

people_and_factions.title: Bríd, the Bride-Peacemaker
people_and_factions.subtitle: [LAW] [FEUD]
people_and_factions.description: Walks between bloodlines with a wooden knife; peace in marriage.
people_and_factions.flavor: Families cut their palms with wood, not iron — blood without a weapon's weight. A Viterran magistrate's confiscated knife is now his letter opener. The Abbess calls the blade 'unconsecrated'; it cuts her robes anyway. Bríd ties a gray thread around the hands of the wed. The knot never loosens. She learned the knot from a Confessor, who learned it from the dead.
people_and_factions.debt: She needs a witness of standing to make a peace binding. Serve as one and she owes the party a future favor.
people_and_factions.price: A blood-price paid in coin, labor, or a public oath.

people_and_factions.title: Matron Eithne
people_and_factions.subtitle: [FAITH] [AUTHORITY]
people_and_factions.description: Queen-mother in truth if not in name; wisdom in water.
people_and_factions.flavor: She drinks only from the ninth well — the one no one admits exists. Shown a dry hole, a Viterran governor believed her. The Abbess's blessing boiled her own hand instead. She has never once told anyone what the ninth well actually looks like. The Confessor comes to her well once a season; she leaves a gray thread, and the Confessor takes it without asking.
people_and_factions.debt: She'll grant a well-blessing (see Rewards, rank 2) to anyone who defends a threshold well from crown or Abbey.
people_and_factions.price: A season's vigil at a well of her choosing.

people_and_factions.title: King Conall
people_and_factions.subtitle: [AUTHORITY] [BALANCE]
people_and_factions.description: Elected by the moots; whale-bone throne, weathered eyes.
people_and_factions.flavor: He lost his left hand to a Linn raid; the replacement is carved from hawthorn. He signs Viterran writs with the false hand — legally binding, though he is not. The Abbess calls him a puppet; the strings are roots. His remaining thumb aches whenever a decision he's avoiding is about to come due. The Gray Liturgy sent him a thread once; he tied it around his wrist and has worn it since. The ache has not returned.
people_and_factions.debt: He owes the moots a decision he's delayed a year. Help him decide, and he grants a royal favor.
people_and_factions.price: Public support for whichever side you help him choose — the other side will remember.

people_and_factions.title: The Lady Beneath
people_and_factions.subtitle: [FAE] [MYSTERY]
people_and_factions.description: Unseen queen who bargains in dreams; hawthorn's whisper.
people_and_factions.flavor: She has no face. Those who see her forget their own names for a year and answer only to 'John.' The Abbess calls her a demon; the demons agree. Where her face should be, there is only the impression of listening. She is patient. She is waiting. The Confessor leaves a thread at her hollow once a year. The thread vanishes. The Lady does not answer — but she listens.
people_and_factions.debt: She keeps every pact ever made with her, perfectly. Breaking one is far more dangerous than making one.
people_and_factions.price: A name — yours, or someone else's. She is never specific about which she wants until the bargain is struck.

complications.title: Ground-Mist
complications.subtitle: [WEATHER] [OMEN]
complications.description: Erases tracks; horns travel, edges do not; navigation by sound alone.
complications.flavor: The mist has a voice. It whispers your name — but only once. A Viterran patrol that entered the mist returned speaking only in questions. An Everflame patrol returned speaking only in confessions. The Confessor walks in willingly, rings her bell, and never says what the mist answers. The Gray Walkers follow the mist's voice to the dead; they sing the keening, and the mist answers in kind.
complications.mechanical_hook: Navigation rolls are Desperate for the scene. On a Miss, a character hears their name called once and must resist (Resolve DV 4) the urge to answer. A gray thread tied to the wrist before entering the mist grants +1 die to resist.

complications.title: Bog-Lights
complications.subtitle: [FAE] [DANGER]
complications.description: Lure a teamster off the causeway; recovery costs time and pride.
complications.flavor: The lights are the souls of those who broke their geas. Follow them, and you'll never find your way back. The Tréadaí follows them singing the keening; the lights lead him to the dead instead of luring him. The Confessor rings her bell when the lights grow bright, and the dead who follow the lights turn away.
complications.mechanical_hook: A character who follows the lights loses 1 segment of travel progress and must roll Wits+Lore (DV 4) to find their way back without further complication. A gray thread left at the point where the lights appeared grants +1 die to the roll.

complications.title: Spoken Geas
complications.subtitle: [TABOO] [CURSE]
complications.description: No ninth word in parley — or the oath curdles like milk.
complications.flavor: The word you cannot speak sits on your tongue like a stone. A Viterran merchant who said 'nine' in a pact now sells only in eights. The Abbess's priest who said it in prayer received an answer he didn't want. The Confessor said it once, rang her bell, and cannot remember the word since. The Gray Liturgy does not speak the ninth word; it ties a thread to the silence instead.
complications.mechanical_hook: Any negotiation scene where a ninth term or clause is spoken aloud voids the deal and ticks the Green Host Rising timer by 1. A gray thread tied before the negotiation allows one ninth word to be spoken without penalty.

complications.title: Salt-Rot
complications.subtitle: [SUPPLY] [CURSE]
complications.description: Smokehouse fails; fish spoil, tempers rise like the tide.
complications.flavor: The salt was cut with grave dust — someone wanted the winter hard. The Confessor salted her own fish with ash from her bell-shrine; it did not rot. The Gray Walkers blessed the salt with a gray thread; the rot did not spread.
complications.mechanical_hook: The affected village loses 1 Supply per day until the cause (a grudge, a curse, or sabotage) is identified and resolved. A gray thread tied to the smokehouse door halts the rot for one day.

complications.title: Procession Clash
complications.subtitle: [FAITH] [TABOO]
complications.description: Saint-day vs. hawthorn taboo; shutters slam, peace fractures.
complications.flavor: The saint's banner and the green branch cannot touch. When they do, blood follows. The Confessor rang her bell between them once, and the crowd parted for her, and no one followed. The Gray Walkers walked between them singing the keening, and the banner and branch turned away from each other.
complications.mechanical_hook: Preventing violence requires a Sway or Insight roll (DV 4) to physically separate the processions before the GM spends 1 SB to escalate to a riot (Cap 2 crowd). A gray thread tied to both banners during the confrontation grants +1 die to the roll.

complications.title: Wave-Count
complications.subtitle: [FAE] [SEA]
complications.description: Eighth swell, Nameless follows; boats tremble, sailors pray.
complications.flavor: The ninth swell never comes. But something rides the eighth. A Viterran customs cutter did not see it; it is at the bottom now. The Tréadaí sails into the eighth swell singing the keening, and the Nameless turns away. The Confessor rings her bell from the shore, and the Nameless listens, but does not answer.
complications.mechanical_hook: Sailing through the eighth swell without a keening or offering forces an Endurance roll (DV 5) or the vessel takes on water — treat as a resource timer tick. A gray thread tied to the prow grants +1 die to the roll.

complications.title: Ringfort Wakes
complications.subtitle: [LAW] [OMEN]
complications.description: A bone-judge is 'consulted'; now you're named in the old law.
complications.flavor: The bone-judge's skull is filled with peat smoke and speaks in riddles and judgments. A Viterran magistrate who ignored its ruling lost his memory of the case entirely. The Confessor asked it a question once; she does not remember the answer. The Gray Walkers consult the bone-judge at dusk; it speaks true, and they sing the keening to silence it.
complications.mechanical_hook: Consulting the bone-judge grants a genuine piece of GM guidance (a hint or true answer), but the questioner forgets one unrelated fact of the GM's choosing. A gray thread left at the skull before asking grants the answer without the cost.

complications.title: Ninth Law
complications.subtitle: [TABOO] [CURSE]
complications.description: Something vital cannot be counted, measured, or named.
complications.flavor: You try to count your crew. The number keeps changing. A Viterran census-taker who tried to count the islanders now lives in a cave, counting seagulls. The Confessor counts her bell-rings and stops at eight. The silence counts. The Gray Liturgy has no count; it ties a thread for every soul and lets the dead keep their own tally.
complications.mechanical_hook: Any roll that depends on an exact count or tally (headcount, inventory, distance) suffers –1 die until the party deliberately leaves the count incomplete or unspoken. A gray thread tied for each item counted grants +1 die to the roll instead.

complications.title: Net-Surge
complications.subtitle: [SEA] [DANGER]
complications.description: Harbor stairs; kelp wraps ankles and alibis like truth.
complications.flavor: The kelp moves against the current. Someone underneath is pulling. A Viterran harbormaster who tried to dredge it is missing; the kelp is thicker now. The Confessor dives for a bell that rang underwater. The kelp loosens. The drowned listen. The Gray Walkers tie a thread to the kelp; it parts for them.
complications.mechanical_hook: Crossing the surging stairs requires Athletics (DV 4); a Miss entangles the character (–1 die on all actions) until freed by an ally. A gray thread tied to the stairs before crossing grants +1 die to the roll.

complications.title: Bride-Theft
complications.subtitle: [FEUD] [LAW]
complications.description: At a moot, peace flips to feud — you're caught mid-ritual.
complications.flavor: The stolen bride's hand is cold; she has been dead for a year. A Viterran sheriff who tried to stop the theft now wears a wedding ring he doesn't remember accepting. The Confessor rings her bell at the wedding, and the dead bride hears, but does not answer. The Gray Walkers sing the keening; the stolen bride's ghost follows the song, and the feud quiets.
complications.mechanical_hook: The party must choose a side (siding with either bloodline grants an ally but starts a **Feud Spiral [6]** timer with the other) or attempt to broker peace via Bríd (Sway DV 5). A gray thread tied to the bride's wrist grants +1 die to the peace roll.

complications.title: Mainland Return
complications.subtitle: [AUTHORITY] [LAW]
complications.description: Exile with papers; elders arrested 'for progress.'
complications.flavor: The papers are stamped with a Viterran seal, still warm and wrong. The arrested elder now works, silent, in the governor's garden. The Confessor offered him a gray thread; he tied it and finally sleeps, though the plants have grown less healthy since. The Gray Walkers freed him once; he chose to return to his garden, thread still tied.
complications.mechanical_hook: Freeing the elder ticks the **Viterran Plantation Timer** down by 1 segment but risks a direct confrontation with crown soldiers (Cap 2). A gray thread tied to the elder's cell door grants +1 die to the escape roll.

complications.title: Green Host Rides
complications.subtitle: [FAE] [CURSE]
complications.description: Hooves like drums, cattle scatter, sentries sleep.
complications.flavor: The riders have no faces — only masks of woven hawthorn. Garrisons that see the Host stand watch or pray at noon and will not explain why. The Tréadaí watches them ride and lights his lantern. They do not look at him. They are not interested in the living — usually. The Confessor rings her bell when the Host rides; the dead who follow the Host hear, and the Host rides on.
complications.mechanical_hook: Every character present must test Resolve (DV 5) or lose their name for the rest of the session (Condition: **Uncounted** — NPCs and other PCs cannot address them by name). A success instead lets the Host answer one question truthfully. A gray thread tied to the wrist before the Host rides grants +1 die to the roll.

complications.title: Great Fog
complications.subtitle: [FAE] [CURSE]
complications.description: Routes loop, bells lie, every promise takes the long way home.
complications.flavor: The fog is old. It remembers vows spoken to the dead and the silence that answered. A Viterran governor who swore to 'pacify' the isles is still lost in it, his dispatches arriving late and making no sense. The Confessor walks into the Great Fog, rings her bell, and it parts for her. She never says where she went. The Gray Walkers follow her thread, sing the keening, and the fog remembers them too.
complications.mechanical_hook: The party is lost until they complete a scene-length ritual act of omission (deliberately not naming something, per the Silent Count) or find a Confessor willing to guide them out. A gray thread tied to a landmark before the fog rolls in grants +1 die to all navigation rolls within the fog.

rewards.title: Well-Blessing
rewards.subtitle: [FAITH] [ONCE]
rewards.description: A named ford crosses you safely, once; water remembers your need.
rewards.flavor: The blessing is a ribbon tied to your wrist — do not tie a ninth knot. A Viterran sheriff's horse refused the blessed ford and had to swim; the Abbess's horse crossed, and drowned. The Confessor blessed this one herself; the ford will recognize your step long after you've forgotten the crossing. She ties a gray thread to every well she blesses, and the wells remember.
rewards.curse_cost: The blessing only works once, and only for the crossing it was granted for. Using it elsewhere voids it entirely.

rewards.title: Moot Token
rewards.subtitle: [LAW] [ONGOING]
rewards.description: An eight-knotted cord; skip any local queue or judgment.
rewards.flavor: The cord is braided from horsehair and silence. Cut a knot to speak. A magistrate who tried to arrest a token-holder found his courtroom empty and the case dismissed. The Confessor's token has nine knots, uncut. She is waiting. The Gray Liturgy's tokens have gray knots; they are never cut, only tied.
rewards.curse_cost: Each knot cut is a favor spent and cannot be untied again. Once all eight are cut, the token's protection ends.

rewards.title: Harbor-Green
rewards.subtitle: [TRADE] [ONGOING]
rewards.description: A painted mark exempts your boat from the next levy; tide as ally.
rewards.flavor: The mark is a circle with an eighth cut — the missing slice is for the Host. A customs officer who tried to board a marked boat now gathers shells on the beach instead. The Gray Liturgy's marks have a gray thread woven into the paint; the tide follows them.
rewards.curse_cost: The mark exempts only one levy. Using it a second time draws direct attention from the crown's customs office.

rewards.title: Hawthorn Pass
rewards.subtitle: [FAE] [ONCE]
rewards.description: Immunity from a single local taboo, for one scene.
rewards.flavor: The pass is a hawthorn twig carried in the mouth — do not chew. An Inquisitor's pyre would not light for a pass-bearer. Keep it in the mouth and it never dries out, no matter how long the journey. The Gray Liturgy's pass has a gray thread tied around it; the taboo does not notice the bearer.
rewards.curse_cost: The immunity lasts one scene only, and the twig must be replaced from a living hawthorn afterward or its protection sours into a minor curse.

rewards.title: Bell-Right
rewards.subtitle: [LAW] [ONGOING]
rewards.description: A lawful ring at a fog-wick summons the watchers; law travels on sound.
rewards.flavor: The bell has no clapper — you must ring it with your own breath. A constable who heard it now refuses to speak of it. The Confessor rings this bell with her breath; the watchers come, and do not speak. The Gray Liturgy keeps a bell at every fog-wick; the watchers know its voice.
rewards.curse_cost: Summoned watchers arrive expecting a genuine emergency. Using the right frivolously damages standing with the moots.

rewards.title: Coracle Share
rewards.subtitle: [TRAVEL] [ONCE]
rewards.description: Crew and oars pledged for one crossing; tide as a steed.
rewards.flavor: The share is a hazel wand, broken in half to claim passage. A governor who tried to seize a coracle share found his hands would not close. The Confessor's own wand always finds water, even in a drought. The Gray Walkers' wands are tied with gray thread; the tide carries them where they need to go.
rewards.curse_cost: The share is good for one crossing only, and the crew expects the wand's other half returned afterward.

rewards.title: Ogham Ruling
rewards.subtitle: [LAW] [ONCE]
rewards.description: A monk's reading settles a dispute in your favor; runes as law.
rewards.flavor: The ruling is carved on a damp slate; the runes may change by morning. A judge who ruled against an Ogham ruling now dreams in runes he cannot read. The Confessor's slate grows a ninth rune at dawn that vanishes by noon. No one has read it. The Gray Liturgy's slates have gray threads tied to them; the runes do not change for those who carry them.
rewards.curse_cost: The ruling is binding only under Brehon law, not Viterran common law — invoking it against the crown carries no legal weight, only moot standing.

rewards.title: Unnumbered Right
rewards.subtitle: [FAE] [DANGEROUS]
rewards.description: Ignore the Ninth prohibition for one action — it binds you to an answer later.
rewards.flavor: The right is a silence. Use it, and the Green Host will ask for its name. A spy who used it now has no shadow; the Host has his name. The Confessor used it once; the bell answered for her, and the Host did not ask. The Gray Liturgy's right is a gray thread tied in a loop — use it, and the Host will ask the Confessor instead.
rewards.curse_cost: The Host's later question must be answered honestly, at a time and place of its choosing — refusal costs the user's own name.

rewards.title: Salt-Cure License
rewards.subtitle: [TRADE] [ONGOING]
rewards.description: Process scarce fish despite ration edicts; preservation as power.
rewards.flavor: The license is signed with a thumbprint that is not yours. A ration officer who refused a licensed boat now eats only ash. The Confessor co-signs these without being asked; no one has caught spoiled fish under her mark yet. The Gray Liturgy's licenses have gray threads woven into the paper; the rot does not reach them.
rewards.curse_cost: The license's true signatory may eventually call in a debt for the use of their thumbprint.

rewards.title: Bride-Charter
rewards.subtitle: [LAW] [ONCE]
rewards.description: Two feuding houses sheath knives for a season; peace in marriage.
rewards.flavor: The charter is written on a wedding veil stained with the first cut of peace. Viterran peace commissioners' copies burn; the Abbess's consecration caught the veil on fire. A gray thread tied to the veil kept it from burning, and the peace held. The Gray Liturgy's charters are tied with gray threads; the peace holds until the thread is cut.
rewards.curse_cost: The truce lasts one season. Afterward, both houses expect a wergild payment from whoever benefited most from the peace.

rewards.title: Private Moot
rewards.subtitle: [LAW] [ONCE]
rewards.description: With the Matron and the King; whispers become policy.
rewards.flavor: The moot is held in a fog hollow. What is spoken there is never written. Spies who tried to listen came away speaking only in fog or in confessions. The Confessor rings her bell at the moot's close, and the fog does not repeat what it heard. The Gray Walkers attend the moot in silence; they carry the dead's votes.
rewards.curse_cost: Attending obligates the party to honor whatever policy emerges, even if it runs counter to their own interests.

rewards.title: Whale-Escort
rewards.subtitle: [TRAVEL] [ONCE]
rewards.description: Eight-oar guards across the Dolmis reach; strength in numbers.
rewards.flavor: The crew carries your name on a scrap of vellum — if it gets wet, you are alone. A warship that tried to intercept a whale-escorted vessel found itself, inexplicably, without a name of its own. The Confessor sails unnamed on purpose; her crew has never needed to call her anything. The Gray Walkers' escort has gray threads on every oar; the Host does not follow them.
rewards.curse_cost: If the vellum is lost or destroyed during the crossing, the escort's protection ends immediately, mid-journey.

rewards.title: Green Favor
rewards.subtitle: [FAE] [DANGEROUS]
rewards.description: One uncanny exception to custom, spoken beneath hawthorn.
rewards.flavor: The favor is a dream. When you wake, the hawthorn will remember — even if you don't. A governor who asked for a Green Favor now believes he is a king; the actual king is amused. The Confessor asked for one, once. She has never said what she dreamed, only that she woke changed. The Gray Liturgy does not ask for Green Favors — it ties a thread to the hawthorn and waits for the favor to ask for itself.
rewards.curse_cost: The favor's exact terms are set by the Host, not the asker, and are revealed only through the dream — which the asker may not fully remember waking.

quick_use_notes.draw_rules: Draw until you have all four suits: Spade = place, Heart = actor, Club = pressure, Diamond = leverage. Highest rank sets the main Timer (2–5 → 4, 6–10 → 6, J/Q/K → 8, A → 10).
quick_use_notes.diamonds: Diamonds are codified outcomes (blessings, tokens, rights) that change position rather than call for a roll.
quick_use_notes.ninth_rule: Whenever a 9 appears in a seed, add an omission to the scene (a missing step, an unsaid name, an unseen guest). If the 9 is a Diamond, the party may break the taboo once — but someone will come to collect later. If a gray thread is tied instead, the Confessor may appear instead.
quick_use_notes.ace_rule: If any Ace appears, echo green-and-count motifs — hawthorn that whispers, bells that miscount, promises that take the long way home. Heart Ace: a Confessor may appear. Spade Ace: a bell-shrine. Club Ace: the Green Host rides. Diamond Ace: the Gray Liturgy offers a thread.

additional_features.silent_count: Players and GMs are encouraged to omit a detail (a name, a step, a tally) when the Ninth appears, echoing Theona's taboo — this is how the islanders evade Viterran law, which cannot count what is not spoken. **Mechanical Effect:** If a player speaks the ninth name/step/item in a scene, tick the **Green Host Rising** timer by 1. If they omit it successfully, gain 1 Boon. If they tie a gray thread instead of speaking, gain 2 Boons and do not tick the timer.
additional_features.green_hosts_omen: Any dream sequence or omen may be framed as the ride of the Green Host — hoofbeats across the sky, wind through the moors, sea spray tasting of salt and blood. The Viterran garrison has learned to ignore the omens (and is understrength for it). The Everflame Inquisitors document them as demonic evidence. The Gray Liturgy interprets them as messages from the dead.
additional_features.bride_peace_feasts: Weddings, truces, and funerals blur; sharing a feast can end a feud for a season — or doom a guest if the ninth cup is poured. The crown has outlawed these feasts; they continue anyway, and crown officers who attend never pour the ninth cup themselves. The Gray Liturgy pours the ninth cup at such feasts — into the ground, for the dead who are always present.
additional_features.gray_thread_mechanic: A character may tie a gray thread around their wrist as a symbol of a burden carried or a promise to a Confessor. The thread cannot be cut by the same hand that tied it. Once per session, the wearer may transfer a Condition caused by guilt, fear, or despair to a willing Confessor NPC, clearing the Condition — the Confessor gains 1 Fatigue. The thread must be burned at a bell-shrine within a week, or the Condition returns.
additional_features.viterran_plantation_timer: **[8 segments]** Tracks the crown's colonization efforts. Advances when the party carries the king's salt (guides a patrol, enforces a writ, speaks against a moot) or a sheriff successfully imposes common law. Retreats when the party supports a moot, hides a fugitive, or exposes a crown official's corruption. At full: a new plantation is declared — a Viterran town is built, lands confiscated, a new sheriff appointed. The Green Host's shadow grows.
additional_features.everflame_orthodoxy_timer: **[6 segments]** Tracks the Abbess's influence. Advances when the party aids the Inquisition, purges 'heresy,' or accepts Everflame gold. Retreats when the party exposes Everflame manipulation, protects native rites, or turns Everflame allies against the Abbess. At full: a permanent tribunal is established, native rites become illegal under penalty of burning, and the Gray Liturgy goes underground.
additional_features.unringing_bell_timer: **[8 segments]** For parties drawn to the Gray Liturgy. Advances when the party breaks a taboo without offering a gray thread, ignores a deathbed confession, or fails to carry a burden. Retreats when the party ties a gray thread, rings a bell-shrine, or helps a Confessor. At full: the Gray Liturgy withdraws its protection entirely — Confessors will not ring, and the dead will not listen.
additional_features.brehon_vs_common_law: In any legal dispute, the party may invoke Brehon law (custom, precedent, witness — +1 die with a respected elder or witnessed oral history) or Viterran common law (statute, seal, written evidence — +1 die with a writ or seal). Choosing one shifts the Viterran Plantation timer accordingly. Relying purely on Taboo instead shifts the Green Host timer. Invoking the Gray Liturgy (a gray thread and a witnessed silence) shifts none of the timers — but the Confessor will remember.

gray_liturgy.name: The Gray Liturgy
gray_liturgy.description: Deep in the mist-shrouded valleys and along the tide-cut stairs of Theona, a different faith endures — one that does not flee the Ninth but approaches it with ritual, witness, and the patient weight of carried secrets. The Gray Liturgy is not a foreign import; it is the old faith that was nearly erased, pushed to the fens and barrows. Its practitioners are not priests. They are keeners (who sing the dead across), well-walkers (who tend the threshold-wells), and taboo-breakers (who have taken the ninth step and returned — changed, but alive). Where Theona's folk practice avoids the Ninth, the Gray Liturgy engages it, ritually and carefully, with witnesses and salt and the Shepherd's lantern. They are not heretics — they are the ones who remember what the Ninth actually is: not a demon, not a curse, but a door left unlocked.

saints_of_the_threshold.irish_name: Naomh Aodhán an Tréadaí (Saint Aodhán the Herdsman)
saints_of_the_threshold.story: Aodhán was a herdsman who lost his flock in a blizzard. He searched three days. On the third night he followed a gray lantern's light to a cave, where his flock waited warm and unharmed. The gray figure said: 'You have found them. Now you will guide those who cannot find their own way.' His feast day is the winter solstice.
saints_of_the_threshold.symbol: A lantern with a single gray flame.
saints_of_the_threshold.invocation: "Aodhán, who found what was lost, guide this soul to the green hills. The snow is deep. The night is long. But your lamp burns."

saints_of_the_threshold.irish_name: Naomh Lasaíocht na gClog (Saint Lasaíocht of the Bells)
saints_of_the_threshold.story: Lasaíocht was a nun who tended the dying in a plague village and carried so many confessions the weight became unbearable. She rang the chapel bell at midnight; it cracked, and the weight fell into the earth. A voice from the bell said: 'You have carried enough. Now you will be the one who carries for others.' Her feast day is the day after Samhain, when the dead are closest.
saints_of_the_threshold.invocation: "Lasaíocht, who rang the bell at midnight, take this burden from my shoulders. Let the earth drink what I cannot swallow. Let the bell ring when I am empty."

saints_of_the_threshold.irish_name: Naomh Ciarán na Cothroime (Saint Ciarán of Balance)
saints_of_the_threshold.story: Ciarán stood seven years in a river, meditating, without moving. When asked how, he said: 'I do not resist the water. I become it. I am not still — I am the stillness between drops.' His feast day is the spring equinox.
saints_of_the_threshold.symbol: A standing stone with a spiral carved into it.
saints_of_the_threshold.invocation: "Ciarán, who stood in the river, steady my breath. The water flows around me, not through me. I am the stone. I am the still point."

saints_of_the_threshold.irish_name: Naomh Fíonntan an Leabhair (Saint Fíonntan of the Book)
saints_of_the_threshold.story: Fíonntan copied every manuscript in his monastery; when Vikings burned the library, he had already memorized every word and spent his life dictating what was lost. His ledger is a book of testimony, not judgment — he records what happened, not what should have. His feast day is the autumn equinox.
saints_of_the_threshold.symbol: An open book with a single gray thread marking a page.
saints_of_the_threshold.invocation: "Fíonntan, who remembered what was burned, witness this crossing. Write the name in your ledger. Do not judge. Do not forgive. Only record. The truth is enough."

saints_of_the_threshold.domain: The forgotten threshold, the unnamed door
saints_of_the_threshold.story: An Caillte was once a saint like the others, but forgot his own name and wandered into the fog. Now he is the Dorcha, the Darkness — not evil, only forgotten. If someone remembers his true name, the Ninth threshold becomes a door instead of a wound. Every year, on the night of the dark moon, he knocks. The Liturgy does not open the door. They wait. They listen. They hope.
saints_of_the_threshold.symbol: An empty circle. A threshold with no door.
saints_of_the_threshold.invocation: "An Caillte, whose name is lost, we do not call you. We cannot call you. But if you remember yourself, knock twice. We will open the door."
saints_of_the_threshold.note: The Liturgy does not invoke An Caillte like the other saints — he is listened for, not called upon. Taboo-Breakers (Caillteoirí) are those who have heard him knock and lived; they alone may approach the Ninth threshold.

saints_of_the_threshold.irish_name: Naomh Scáthach na Seift (Saint Scáthach of the Cunning)
Naomh Maolmhuire na dTost (Saint Maolmhuire of Silences)

practices.name: The Ninth Cup Ritual
practices.irish_name: Deoch na gCuig (Cup of the Ninth)
practices.description: Poured at the dark moon onto a grave. If the earth drinks, the dead are at peace. If the water pools, the dead are restless.

practices.name: The Confession of the Dying
practices.description: The dying speak every secret. The Confessor listens and rings a small iron bell once. The weight transfers.

practices.name: The Well-Walk
practices.irish_name: Siúilóid an Tobair (Walk of the Well)
practices.description: Descent into a sacred well until dawn. If you emerge, you have seen the Ninth and returned.

practices.name: The Keening
practices.description: A wordless melody that guides the dead. The Gray Walker sings; the dead follow.

practices.name: The Gray Thread
practices.description: Tied around the wrist of the dying; cut when they pass. The thread is burned at the Ninth Cup Ritual.

practices.name: The Bell-Shrine
practices.irish_name: Clochán na gClog (Stone of the Bells)
practices.description: A small stone hut where a bell hangs. Confessors ring it when a burden is transferred.

sprinkle_cards.description: Additional cards for GMs running Gray Liturgy-heavy scenes — sprinkle into draws alongside the standard 13-card suits rather than replacing them.

places.title: Clochán na gClog (Bell-Shrine)
places.description: A small stone hut on a misty headland holding a single cracked, silent bell. Confessors ring it when a burden is transferred. The crown declared it a nuisance; it rings anyway. The Abbess's attempt to melt it down went cold in the forge.

places.title: Tobar an Chaillte (Well of the Lost One)
places.description: A sacred well no one admits exists. The water is black and still. Taboo-Breakers drink from it before a Well-Walk. Neither surveyors nor clerics can find it on any map. The Lady Beneath drinks from it too.

people.title: Clogaire (a Confessor)
people.description: A bell-ringer who carries the weight of the dead. Her hands are scarred from ringing. She never speaks of what she has heard.

people.title: Tréadaí (a Gray Walker)
people.description: A guide for the dying, carrying a lantern with a single gray flame, singing the keening at deathbeds.

complications.title: The Unsung Bell (1 SB)
complications.description: A confession is not enough. The Confessor cannot ring her bell. The weight must be carried until a witness volunteers.

complications.title: The Ninth Knock (2 SB)
complications.description: An Caillte knocks at the threshold. A door that was closed now rattles. The Gray Liturgy waits. The Green Host listens.

complications.title: The Burdened Confessor (3 SB)
complications.description: A Confessor collapses under the weight of unspoken sins. She cannot ring. She cannot speak. She can only wait for someone to carry her.

rewards.title: Bell-Ringer's Blessing
rewards.description: Once, ignore a Condition caused by guilt or despair. The Confessor rings her bell for you, flat and mournful and final.

rewards.title: Gray Thread
rewards.description: A gray thread tied around your wrist. Cut it to transfer a burden to a willing Confessor. The thread cannot be cut by the same hand that tied it.

lore_echoes.title: Saint Bríd of the Unquenched Well (Syncretic)
lore_echoes.description: A local saint venerated by both the Temple of Light and the old well-keepers. Her shrine is a well hung with red ribbons; pilgrims who tie an eighth knot and leave a silver coin may ask one question of the Green Host — but the answer comes in a dream, and the dream always takes a memory. The Viterran bishop has declared her a heretic three times; each declaration was found burned. The Gray Liturgy leaves a gray thread at her well every spring; the Confessor says she hears the answers the dead give.

lore_echoes.title: Saint Colmán of the Eighth Bell (Oath of Mercy and Grace)
lore_echoes.description: A missionary who tried to convert the isles by ringing a ninth bell. The Green Host took his tongue, and he spent his life speaking only in eights. His hospice near the Fog-Wick Tower heals the fog-sick, but every patient leaves unable to count past eight. The Gray Liturgy tends his hospice; they tie a thread to every patient's wrist, and the counting returns.

lore_echoes.title: The Dullahan (The Headless Horseman)
lore_echoes.description: A fae omen that rides when a Viterran sheriff is about to die, carrying its own head under its arm and calling the sheriff's name. Those who hear it are dead before dawn. The Gray Liturgy's Walkers sing the keening when the Dullahan rides; the headless rider turns away from the dying.

lore_echoes.title: The Banshee (Bean Sidhe)
lore_echoes.description: A spirit who keens when a pure-blooded Theona chieftain dies. The crown has tried to suppress her songs as 'noise pollution.' The keening continues; the chieftains die. The Gray Liturgy's Walkers sing with the Banshee; the dead listen more kindly.

lore_echoes.title: The Morrígan (The Phantom Queen)
lore_echoes.description: A war goddess who appears as a crow before battle. She does not choose sides — she chooses the dead. Viterran soldiers who see a crow before a skirmish often desert. The Gray Liturgy's Truth-Tellers record which battles she favored; their ledgers are written in gray ink, and the names are never forgotten.

lore_echoes.title: The Ninth
lore_echoes.description: In any Theona scene, the ninth person to speak in a room draws the Green Host's attention. The wise hold their tongues until someone else breaks the count. Those who speak ninth are said to see a pale rider on the horizon the next night. The Gray Liturgy's Confessors are the ninth speaker by choice; they carry the weight of the attention so others do not.

superstitions.name: Bread to the Bog
superstitions.effect: Toss a crust into the mist before crossing a causeway. Ignore the first Ground-Mist penalty.

superstitions.name: Knot the Eighth
superstitions.effect: Tie a single knot in a ribbon before a moot. Cancel Spoken Geas or take –1 die on your next oath (your choice).

superstitions.name: Name to the Well
superstitions.effect: Whisper a dead enemy's name into Saint's Well. Gain +1 Effect against his kin for the scene, but the Matron — and the Abbess — will remember your name.

superstitions.name: Thread to the Confessor
superstitions.effect: Tie a gray thread around your wrist before a dangerous journey. Once, transfer a Condition from fear or despair to a Confessor (she carries it; the thread turns black — burn it at a bell-shrine).

superstitions.name: Step of the Uncounted
superstitions.effect: Before crossing a threshold, take eight steps and pause. The ninth step is not taken — it is left for the Host. Gain +1 die to the first action after crossing.

minor_complications: **Exposure:** Your actions draw unwanted attention from **moot-keepers, well-guardians, Viterran sheriffs, Everflame clerics, or Gray Liturgy Confessors**.
**Noise:** Sounds of your actions alert nearby **coracle crews, ringfort sentries, crown patrols, Inquisitor spies, or keeners**.
**Trace:** Evidence of your passage marks your route for **trackers, green neighbors, crown informers, Host riders, or Confessors**.
**Delay:** A brief but meaningful setback costs you time or favorable tide.
**Supply Strain:** Mark +1 segment on a relevant resource timer.
**Unsung Confession (Gray Liturgy):** A Confessor cannot ring her bell. The weight must be carried until a witness volunteers.
moderate_setbacks: **Alarm Raised:** Wick-warden, moot official, Viterran bailiff, Everflame novice, or Gray Walker becomes aware and begins responding.
**Position Lost:** You lose advantageous ground/cover/stealth due to mist shift, taboo breach, a roadblock, a ward, or a keening.
**Foe Appears:** A feuding house member, bone-judge, crown soldier, Everflame penitent, or Confessor arrives on scene.
**Gear Trouble:** A piece of equipment becomes Compromised/Neglected.
**Lock/Barrier:** A simple obstacle now requires a test to overcome.
**The Ninth Knock:** An Caillte knocks at a threshold. A door that was closed now rattles.
serious_trouble: **Reinforcements:** Additional coracle crews, green neighbors, moot enforcers, crown militia, Everflame zealots, or Gray Liturgy Witnesses arrive.
**Key Gear Breaks:** A crucial tool/weapon becomes temporarily unusable.
**Major Twist:** The situation fundamentally changes — taboo broken/Green Host rides/feud declared/crown warrant issued/Inquisition summons/Gray Liturgy withdraws.
**Rail Tick:** Advance a relevant campaign/front timer by 1 segment.
**Condition Applied:** Mark Fatigue 1/Harm 1/Condition appropriate to fiction.
**The Burdened Confessor:** A Confessor collapses under the weight of unspoken sins. She cannot ring. She cannot speak.
major_turns: **Trap Springs:** A prepared danger activates with full effect.
**Authority Arrival:** King, Matron, Lady Beneath, Viterran Governor, Abbess of Whiterick, or High Confessor intervenes.
**Scene Shift:** The environment changes dramatically — fog rises/bells ring/causeway shifts/crown forces arrive/Great Fog rolls in.
**Patron Omen:** Divine/arcane forces take notice — omen appears/blessing lost/curse manifests/Host rides/An Caillte knocks.
**Narrative Pivot:** The story takes an unexpected turn that reframes objectives.
**The Unringing Bell:** The Gray Liturgy withdraws its protection. Confessors will not ring. The dead will not listen.
region_specific: **Theona (Silent Count):** Steps disappear mid-climb, names vanish from lips, the ninth item in a list goes unmentioned, a gray thread tightens on a wrist.
**Theona (Green Host):** Hoofbeats echo without a horse, mist takes familiar shapes, dreams predict the next action, a Confessor rings her bell.
**Theona (Viterran Law):** A writ is declared void, a sheriff's seal cracks, a witness remembers the ninth name, a plantation is surveyed.
**Theona (Everflame Orthodoxy):** A prayer is answered wrongly, a brand burns without fire, a confession is heard by the wrong ears, an Inquisition is called.
**Theona (Gray Liturgy):** A bell rings without a ringer, a gray thread tightens on a wrist, a Confessor's shadow stretches toward the dead, An Caillte knocks.

pursuit_ladder.effect: On a hit, shift one range band. On a strong hit, also impose Fog Bank.
On a hit, freeze range for one exchange; if a moot token is in your possession, +1 die.
On a hit during Green Host Rides, you pick who is named; on a Miss, the GM does.
On a hit, hide a taboo act from the Inquisition; on a Miss, gain the Condition Marked for Purity.
On a hit during a Gray Liturgy scene, transfer a Condition to a willing Confessor; on a Miss, the Confessor cannot ring — the weight doubles.
On a hit during a taboo scene, tie a gray thread instead of speaking a ninth name; gain +1 die on the next roll. On a Miss, the thread is cut — the Confessor will not answer.

boss_archetypes.name: The Unsung Bell
boss_archetypes.description: A forbidden note given will — a bell that should never have rung a ninth time.
cracks: bind its clapper with eight ribbons
let a rival speak the ninth and pay the price instead
drown the echo at the Sea-Cave Harp
**Gray Liturgy variant:** let a Confessor ring it once — it will shatter or sing, and no one knows which

boss_archetypes.name: Bride-Thief of the Green Host
boss_archetypes.description: A dream raider of the Host, come to claim a bride who never agreed to the marriage.
cracks: cut the dream-veil with silver
sing satire at the Green Moot Hill
trade a Bride-Charter
**Gray Liturgy variant:** offer a gray thread instead of a bride — the Host may accept, tying it around the King in Green's wrist instead

boss_archetypes.name: The Sheriff's Black Assize
boss_archetypes.description: A Viterran enforcer escalating from decree to hanging.
cracks: produce a witnessed Brehon judgment older than the crown's claim
make the kin-whole with cattle, not counted coin
let the Green Host take his name
**Gray Liturgy variant:** tie a gray thread around the noose — the rope will not tighten

boss_archetypes.name: The Abbess's Golden Inquisition
boss_archetypes.description: An Everflame purifier escalating from doctrine to brand.
cracks: expose her pact with raiders
turn her own clerics against her with truth
let the Green Host ride during the trial
**Gray Liturgy variant:** ring a Confessor's bell in the cathedral — the Abbess will hear, and will not confess, but the bell rings anyway

boss_archetypes.name: The Missing Step
boss_archetypes.description: A living omission — a vanished witness, an unread clause, an unwalkable bridge.
cracks: invite a Taboo-Witness to count aloud
spill nine drops into Saint's Well but name only eight
let the Lady Beneath keep a memory
**Gray Liturgy variant:** step where the step is missing — you will fall, land on a gray thread, and be pulled back by a Confessor, though you won't remember where you fell

patronage_and_power: In Theona, power flows through ancient custom, sacred spaces, and the careful observance of taboo. The Three Greens maintain their independence through a web of moots, well-keepers, and geas-keepers who ensure the old laws are honored. The King and Matron rule by consensus and tradition, while the unseen Lady Beneath influences events through dreams and whispers. Against them stands the Viterran crown — sheriffs, bishops, and undertakers who seek to replace Brehon law with common law, hawthorn with church stone, and the Green Host with the White Flame. And watching from Whiterick Abbey, the Everflame Abbess schemes to preserve power by pitting Viterra, the native factions, and raiders against each other. In the mist, a quieter power waits: the Gray Liturgy does not scheme — it rings, it carries, it listens. Its Confessors hold the weight of the dead; its Gray Walkers guide the dying across; its Well-Walkers descend into the Ninth and return. It offers no gold, no land, no writs — only a gray thread and a cracked bell. For those who have lost too much, that is enough. **For the GM:** tie rewards to visible symbols (ribbons, tokens, blessings, gray threads) that can be challenged, stolen, or voided by crown officials; let the crown, the Host, the Abbess, and the Gray Liturgy grant conflicting protections so players must choose whose favor matters more; use moots, wells, and causeways as arenas for social contests weighing Brehon law against Viterran common law and Everflame orthodoxy; and remember the Viterran Plantation, Everflame Orthodoxy, and Unringing Bell timers are visible campaign fronts — once they fill, the isles change forever. The Gray Liturgy's timer is the quietest, and the most patient.
